p: The navigation system uses a responsive top navigation bar for desktop screens and a collapsible hamburger menu for mobile viewports. The navigation bar contains the application logo or brand name on the left side and navigation links on the right side. Authentication state determines which links are visible with login and register links shown for unauthenticated users and profile and logout links shown for authenticated users.

The main layout wrapper provides consistent spacing and structure across all pages. A container div centers content with maximum width constraints for readability. The layout automatically adjusts padding based on viewport size using responsive utility classes. The footer contains copyright information and links to privacy policy and terms of service pages.

Breadcrumb navigation is implemented on detail pages to show the user their current location within the application hierarchy. Each breadcrumb segment is a clickable link except for the current page segment which is rendered as plain text. Breadcrumbs improve navigation efficiency and reduce user disorientation in multi-level page structures.

All forms follow a consistent design pattern with labeled input fields, validation messages, and submit buttons. Input fields display a focus ring when selected for accessibility. Validation messages appear below the relevant field in red text immediately when the field loses focus with invalid data. Submit buttons show a loading spinner during API requests to indicate processing state.

File upload input components support drag-and-drop file selection in addition to the standard file picker dialog. Upload preview shows the selected image before submission. File type and size validation occurs on the client side before upload to provide immediate feedback and reduce unnecessary server requests. Upload progress is displayed during file transfer.

Select dropdowns use a custom styled component for consistent appearance across different browsers. Searchable select fields allow filtering options by typing for large option sets. Multi-select fields use tag-style display for selected values with individual removal capability. All select components support keyboard navigation for accessibility compliance.

Data tables display tabular information with sortable columns and pagination controls. Column headers are clickable to toggle ascending and descending sort order with visual indicators showing the current sort direction. Pagination controls show page numbers and total record count with previous and next navigation buttons. The table is horizontally scrollable on narrow viewports.

Card components display individual items in a grid layout with consistent sizing and spacing. Each card shows a thumbnail image, title, brief description, and key metadata. Cards are clickable and navigate to the detail page. Hover effects provide visual feedback with subtle elevation changes and shadow intensification.

Detail pages show comprehensive information about a single resource with organized sections for different information categories. Related resources are displayed at the bottom of the detail page for cross-navigation. Action buttons for edit and delete operations are positioned in the page header for authenticated users with appropriate permissions.

The minimum Node.js version requirement is 18.0.0 or higher with npm 9.0.0 or higher for package management. The application has been tested with Node.js 18.x and 20.x LTS releases. MongoDB version 6.0 or higher is required for the database layer with MongoDB Atlas providing the recommended managed database service.

Frontend build requirements include a modern web browser supporting ES modules and CSS Grid layout. Supported browsers include the latest versions of Chrome, Firefox, Safari, and Edge. Internet Explorer is not supported. The application uses progressive enhancement for features that are not available in older browser versions.

Hardware requirements for development include a minimum of 8GB RAM and a multi-core processor. Production deployment requirements vary based on expected traffic volume. A single server instance with 2GB RAM and 2 CPU cores supports moderate traffic. Horizontal scaling with load balancing supports increased traffic volumes for production deployments.

The backend uses Express.js version 4.x with Mongoose version 7.x or 8.x for MongoDB object modeling. Additional backend dependencies include bcryptjs version 2.4.x for password hashing, jsonwebtoken version 9.x for JWT generation and verification, cors for cross-origin support, helmet for security headers, express-mongo-sanitize for NoSQL injection prevention, and compression for response optimization.

The frontend uses React version 18.x with React Router DOM version 6.x for client-side routing. The Vite build tool version 5.x provides the development server and production build pipeline. Tailwind CSS version 3.x provides utility-first styling. Axios version 1.x handles HTTP communication with the backend API.

Development tools include Nodemon for automatic server restarts during development, ESLint with the Airbnb style guide for code quality enforcement, Prettier for consistent code formatting, and Husky for git hook management. These tools ensure code quality and consistency across the development team.

All API responses follow a consistent JSON structure with a success boolean indicator. Successful responses include a data field containing the requested resource or resource array. Paginated responses include a pagination object with page, limit, totalPages, and totalResults fields for client-side pagination handling.

Error responses include a success field set to false and an error object containing a message field with a human-readable error description. Validation errors include an additional errors array with field-level error objects containing field and message properties. This structured error format enables consistent error handling across the frontend application.

The API uses standard HTTP status codes for response status indication. 200 for successful GET and PUT requests, 201 for successful POST requests, 204 for successful DELETE requests, 400 for validation errors, 401 for authentication failures, 403 for authorization denials, 404 for resource not found, 409 for duplicate resource conflicts, and 500 for server errors.
